question: On which of the following dates did the Muslim League decide to join the Interim Government?
solution:
The correct answer is __**13 October 1946.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​​A **political organisation called the All-India Muslim League (AIML) **was founded in British India in 1906. The party was created in response to the necessity for **Muslim political participation in British India,** particularly in the case of strong Hindu resistance to the 1905 partition of Bengal, which was supported by the **Indian National Congress**.
 
• The **league's goals** were to instil in Muslims a sense of allegiance to the** British government.**
 
• To** protect Muslims' political rights** and to express such rights to the government. To stop Muslims from developing prejudice toward other** Indian communities. **
 
• On October 25, 1946, **five members of the Muslim League **were sworn in as part of the newly constituted Interim Government. They were given the** Finance Department.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In the 1940s, the** League was crucial to the struggle for Indian independence.** It served as one of the impetuses for the establishment of Pakistan as a **Muslim state on the Indian continent.**
 
• The** Muslim League was divided **after India and Pakistan gained their independence.
 
• 
 
The** 48th Imam of Ismaili Shia Muslims **was His Highness Sir Sultan Muhammed Shah, Aga Khan III GCSI GCMG GCIE GCVO PC. He served as the** All-India Muslim League's first president**. On November 2, 1877, he was born in Karachi, and on July 11, 1957, he died in Versoix, **Switzerland. **
